title: Entralink room
description: One room of the Entralink roguelike (docs/paperwhite2/design/entralink-roguelike-prototype.md, The room format): the rounds it is kept to, its role, its weather, its battles and the NPCs standing in it. Its ID is the file's name. Edited in the editor's Entree page; tools/paperwhite2/entralink_run.py checks it and packs it for the game.

name.description: The room's name, for the editor

progress_id.description: A room's record id (rooms/ only; a template has none): its discovered and beaten bits and its boss record in the save, unique over all rooms and never changed or reused once given (the editor gives the next of progress_ids.json's next_room on save)

rounds.description: The rounds of a run it is kept to, each once: 1 before the first boss, 2 before the second, 3 before the final room. Left out, it can come up in any round

role.description: room: a room of a round. boss: the room ending round 1 or 2, from the bosses' own pool. final: the run's last room

type.description: A room of role room: what kind of room it is, which a door draws by its round's type_weights (run.json) and whose marker the door shows (enemy, enemy_choice, challenge, rest, gift for item and buff, shop, event); enemy if left out. An enemy room has one battle, an enemy_choice room several to choose from, one NPC each. A premade rest, item, buff or shop room comes up instead of its type's template (templates/<type>.json) at run.json's custom_chance. A template's type is its file's (pre_boss_rest's rest). Boss and final rooms ignore it

weather.description: Its battles' weather from their start (constants/battle.h; BTL_WEATHER_NONE for clear); the field keeps its round's fog (run.json). Left out, the battles take the field's

marker.description: The marker on the ground in front of any door leading to it (markers/<marker>.png); left out, a room's by its type (enemy, enemy_choice, challenge, rest, gift for item and buff, shop, event), a boss or final room's by its role (boss, final). unknown always shows ???. The game shows catch instead of enemy, enemy_choice, challenge or boss while one of its enemies can be caught and the run's bag holds a Nightmare Ball

battles.description: Its battles, each started by the battle NPCs that name it

npcs.description: What stands in the room. If none spawns, the room is free and the player goes on

message_style.description: The window its message shows in: talk (the default), the talk balloon with its tail at the NPC (ActorMsg); bubble, the tailless balloon across the bottom of the screen (InfoMsg); yell, the spiky balloon at the NPC, which shakes (ActorMsg's spiky frame); event, the system window (SystemMsg)

id.description: Its name in the room, which battle NPCs name it by

progress_id.description: Its won-ever bit in the save, unique over all rooms' battles and never changed or reused once given (the editor gives the next of progress_ids.json on save)

format.description: single: one enemy. double: one or two. triple: one to three. raid: exactly one, in the center of a triple battle against three of the player's Pokémon

scale.description: Its own multiplier in percent on top of run.json's enemy_scaling, on every stat, for an enemy that comes out too easy or too hard; 100 if left out

moves.description: Its moves, in order, replacing the ones it has by its level (the run's difficulty tier's, run.json's tiers)

ability.description: An ABILITY_* it has whatever its species', or "hidden" for its hidden one; without it, one of its species' two

item.description: Its held item; none if left out

gender.description: As its species allows; random if left out

catch.description: Left out, it can't be caught. With it, it can, with the Nightmare Ball only (always caught when allowed); a capture counts as winning the battle

after.description: The battles, as "<room id>/<battle id>", that must have been won at least once (in any run, or earlier in this one) before it can be caught; empty or left out, from the first encounter

once.description: true (the default): once caught, it can never be caught again

progress_id.description: A catchable enemy's caught-ever bit in the save, unique over all rooms' catches and never changed or reused once given (the editor gives the next of progress_ids.json on save)

type.description: battle: starts the battle it names. item: gives a fixed item. heal: heals every Pokémon that hasn't fainted (HP, status, PP). revive: revives a fainted Pokémon the player chooses, to full HP. gift: a choice of 3 random items of items.json's gift pool. shop: a shop, the Poké Mart's screen selling run.json's shop_items items of items.json's shop pool for Dream Dust into the run's bag; talking to it is the room's choice, and it opens again after. item_choice: an item ball whose item is drawn from items.json's item_room pool as the room is entered, its bag icon floating above it. buff_choice: a buff ball (a placeholder line for now). swap: for run.json's swap_dust in Dream Dust, brings a Pokémon of the Reserve Box (set in the hub) into the team as a level 100 copy, in place of a copy that hasn't fainted, which leaves the run. ambient: an actor with nothing to say that reacts when the player comes near (behaviour, near, return, far, distance): it fades out, or runs away and fades; several may stand in a room (decoys round its real battle NPC), and they never keep a room from being done. rest and buff: their before dialogue only (the old placeholders). Using one heal, revive, gift, shop, item_choice or swap NPC is the room's choice: the room's other NPCs of those types go and the room is done; its battle NPCs stay, optional

battle.description: A battle NPC's battle, by its id; several NPCs may start the same one

enemy.description: A battle NPC: the enemy of its battle (0 the first) whose overworld sprite it shows and whose cry it plays; 0 if left out

item.description: An item NPC's item; an item_choice NPC's is drawn, never set

count.description: How many of its item it gives; 1 if left out

sprite.description: Its overworld sprite. Without it a battle NPC shows its enemy's walking Pokémon, item and item_choice NPCs the item ball (OBJ_CODE_110), a buff_choice NPC the buff ball, the others the Lady (OBJ_CODE_LADY)

requires.description: It spawns only after all of these: "<room id>/<battle id>", that battle won at least once in any run, and "run/completed", the final room beaten at least once; empty or left out, always

chance.description: Its chance to spawn, in percent; 100 if left out

x.description: Its tile, 0-31 from the room's left; every forest clearing has the same 32 by 32 grid and exits

z.description: Its tile, 0-31 from the room's top

marker.description: An icon floating above its head, by name: npc_markers/<marker>.png; none if left out

behaviour.description: An ambient's reaction when the player comes within near tiles: fade, it fades out where it stands (over about 15 frames); flee, it turns and runs distance tiles away from the player, fading as it goes, then is gone. fade if left out

near.description: An ambient: how close the player comes (tiles either way) before it reacts; 3 if left out

return.description: A fading ambient: it comes back (fading in at its tile) once the player is far tiles away again; without it, it is gone for the rest of the room

far.description: A returning ambient: how far the player goes (tiles either way) before it comes back; more than near; 6 if left out

distance.description: A fleeing ambient: the tiles it runs away (fewer where its way is blocked); 4 if left out

dialogue.description: What it says, in the text files' codes ({be01} a wait, {be00} a new page after one, ...); the build compiles every room's into a text bank. Missing or empty: nothing

before.description: On talking to it; a battle NPC's before its battle starts

after.description: A battle NPC's, after its battle is won, before the room opens; other types ignore it
